McLaren: McLaren’s rear wing now carries extra “furniture” – small aerodynamic pieces that smooth the airflow over the wing. This tweak should give the car a cleaner rear‑end down‑force, helping it stick to the track better in the high‑speed corners. In short, the extra wing elements are meant to boost grip and stability, which could translate into quicker lap times and a stronger fight for podium spots this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has trimmed the central winglet on the rear wing and added a small winglet behind the exhaust, both aimed at shaving drag so the car can pull more speed down the long straights of this circuit. At the front, the lip has been reshaped to smooth the airflow into the tyres, giving the car better bite in the corners. Together these tweaks should boost straight‑line pace without sacrificing the down‑force needed for a strong qualifying and race performance.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has reinforced the rear‑wheel bodywork, fixing a weak spot that could have caused reliability hiccups, so the car should stay on the track longer without losing grip. They’ve also reshaped the “floor bib” – the edge where the floor meets the chassis – to smooth the airflow and recover a little extra down‑force. Together, these tweaks mean a more stable, trouble‑free run this weekend, giving the drivers a better chance to push the limits in qualifying and the race.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has reshaped the rear‑top wishbone’s rear leg fairing, tweaking how the suspension handles the forces coming off the rear tyres. The change gives the car a more stable rear end and smoother load transfer, which should improve grip and tyre wear, especially through the slower corners. In short, it’s a subtle aero‑suspension tweak that can translate into better corner exit speed and consistency for this weekend’s race.
